key_insight: Adaptive mesh neural operators need to decide not only where to sample PDE space, but also how to align representations after node relocation so aggregation remains physically meaningful.
engineering_relevance: GA-AMNO provides a more inspectable and robust path for scientific ML solvers on nonuniform meshes, especially when geometric mismatch makes cross-discretization communication unstable.
method: Physics-informed adaptive allocation chooses where to compute.
Geometry-conditioned low-rank Gauge transport maps source features into target representation contexts before aggregation.
Operator readability separates allocation effects from interaction effects and supports interventions.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on five PDE benchmarks, where it improves predictive accuracy and controlled mismatch tests show better cross-discretization compatibility.
watch_item: Gauge transport adds geometric modeling and low-rank approximation complexity, so performance may depend on preserving topology and correctly estimating transport under strong mesh deformation.
paper_title: Where to Compute and How to Interact: Operator-Readable Adaptation with Gauge-Aware Transport
